properties.title: Scaling Recurrence-aware Foundation Models for Clinical Records via Next-Visit Prediction

properties.version_basis: PDF identified by SHA-256 against assignments.json; title page read.

properties.description: Recurrence-aware next-visit generative pretraining on structured EHR, with zero-shot horizon-conditioned disease onset queries, scaling study and external EHRSHOT transfer.

Visit-level decoder transformer over 42,337 EHR tokens predicting the full event set of the next visit from history and elapsed time, queried with a future-time separator token for disease onset risk.

properties.algorithm: 144M-parameter visit-level causal transformer with weighted multi-label binary cross-entropy and history-dependent recurrence weights

properties.population: adult health-system patients with structured records
properties.decision: risk stratification over a specified horizon, not absolute risk

properties.description: NYU Langone held-out test patients, 193,237 of about 1.29 million
EHRSHOT Stanford test patients, N 2,212, zero-shot transfer with lossy concept mapping
Zero-shot onset forecasting at 2 and 5 years on held-out NYU data, demographic restriction, calibration, operating points and EHRSHOT transfer

properties.algorithm: Joint gap and event generation model (EGE)
Logistic regression and GBM on demographic and utilization covariates

relation_assertions.rationale: A learned next-visit predictor queried for horizon-conditioned onset risk, with no actions or controller.
Reviewer mapping: visit-history state and a learned next-visit transition.
Reviewer mapping: visit-history state and a learned next-visit transition.

capability_assessments.rationale: One-step next-visit and horizon-queried predictions are evaluated on held-out and external patients, which meets L1. There are no actions, so L2 is not met. Visit history is carried into each prediction with learned temporal dynamics, which meets the V11 core membership criteria, although the authors note only one-step prediction has been used.

One-step next-visit and horizon-queried predictions are evaluated on held-out and external patients, which meets L1. There are no actions, so L2 is not met. Visit history is carried into each prediction with learned temporal dynamics, which meets the V11 core membership criteria, although the authors note only one-step prediction has been used.

gate_assessments.rationale: Patient-level 70/15/15 NYU splits, 1-year gap window, and history-label exclusion are implemented, but feature availability times are not reported (data.availability_time) and external EHRSHOT transfer uses lossy code mapping retaining only ~25% of rows (p. 18).

Carried visit history (state.persistent), time-coded next-visit transitions (dynamics.temporal), and held-out/external zero-shot predictions (rollout.one_step_evaluated) are evaluated on 193,237 NYU and 2,212 EHRSHOT patients against rollout, LLM, fine-tuned BERT, and demographic baselines (Tables 1-2, Figs. 2-3).
No sequential rollout of RAVEN is evaluated, and horizon-query scores are not monotone in many windows.

legacy_cells.B: Scaling Recurrence-aware Foundation Models for Clinical Records via Next-Visit Prediction
legacy_cells.C: Gao, Xiang, Rajamohan, Haresh Rengaraj, Zhu, Weicheng, Huang, Shih-Lun, Chen, Long, Schulman, Gabe, et al.
legacy_cells.O: Dementia; knee osteoarthritis; pancreatic cancer; prostate cancer; acute myocardial infarction; congestive heart failure; chronic obstructive pulmonary disease; lupus; hyperlipidemia; hypertension; celiac disease
legacy_cells.S: Whether a patient's history predicts first onset of selected conditions within a future 2- or 5-year horizon (1-year tasks in EHRSHOT).
legacy_cells.T: De-identified NYU Langone longitudinal EHR patients (1,288,242; 2013–2023; median 21 visits); external EHRSHOT test cohort of 2,212 patients from Stanford.
legacy_cells.X: F2 EHR / ICU event & latent patient dynamics
legacy_cells.AI: Structured longitudinal EHR events: demographics (race, ethnicity, sex), age, diagnoses (ICD-10), prescribed medications, laboratory codes and values (LOINC)
legacy_cells.AJ: Decoder-only GPT-2-based Transformer; 8 layers, 8 attention heads, hidden dimension 1024, maximum sequence length 512 (main model).
legacy_cells.BS: Predicted multi-label set of clinical-event tokens for the next visit (diagnoses, medications, laboratory results, and demographics); disease-risk scores are pooled from condition-code logits.
legacy_cells.BT: Linear projection and sigmoid for next-visit token probabilities; condition-specific zero-shot score pools logits across the disease code set and applies sigmoid.
legacy_cells.BV: Weighted binary cross-entropy for next-visit multi-label prediction; positive target weights decay as λ raised to the prior-history occurrence count, with minimum weight; main setting λ⋆=0.5.
legacy_cells.BX: Pretrained on NYU Langone records from 1,288,242 patients.
legacy_cells.BY: Main model: 144 million parameters; scaling configurations 0.69 million to 848.80 million parameters.
legacy_cells.CR: Calibration evaluated using Brier score, Brier skill score, and expected calibration error at 2- and 5-year horizons; Platt scaling and isotonic recalibration were fit on validation and evaluated on test data.
legacy_cells.FN: RAVEN zero-shot macro-average AUROC was 0.780 at two years and 0.752 at five years; at two years the structured next-token/simulation baselines scored 0.642, 0.662 and 0.626, and MedGemma 0.659. External transfer was evaluated under lossy ontology/feature mapping.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M3 Belief-state service; M5 Dynamics adapter; M7 Outcome & causal layer
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Expose future-state forecasts through a time-aware dynamics interface and validate error versus horizon; treatment actions need separate evidence before intervention simulation.
legacy_cells.FX: PDF title and abstract (p. 1); Introduction and overview (pp. 2–4); primary results, figures, and main forecasting tables (pp. 4–16); Methods, cohort, architecture, training objective, inference, evaluation metrics, and calibration (pp. 17–23); availability statements (p. 24); relevant calibration and operating-point supplementary tables (pp. 37–41). Complete 43-page extracted text was available; all evidence-bearing methods and results used above were reviewed. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: A:I retained as prefilled; no PDF contradiction requiring correction. M is not applicable because the record is included. RAVEN's results establish one-step, horizon-conditioned predictive scoring only; no treatment-action conditioning, causal identification, counterfactual comparison, or planning is demonstrated. The model's medication history tokens are observed EHR events, not intervention inputs. The main forecasting tables and relevant calibration tables were legible in extracted text; the garbled layout of unrelated supplementary table S15 was not relied upon. Evidence QA: 34/44 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (77.3%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. limitations: All 43 PDF pages were read as extracted text (including Table 3 on p. 18, References on pp. 25-26, and Supplementary Tables S1-S18 and Figs. S1-S4 captions on pp. 27-43), and rendered page images were visually inspected for pages 3, 5, 6, 7, 9, and 13 (Figs. 1-3, 6; Tables 1-2).

Main visual figures 4, 5, and 7 and supplementary figure images S1-S4 were not separately rendered as PNGs; their full numeric tables (Tables S1-S18) and captions were read directly from extracted text.
The legacy row was read from the root workbook (read only). Saved API drafts for B103 were not opened.
Schema validity and quote occurrence do not establish semantic correctness. One reviewer pass, no independent human review.
notes: RAVEN is a visit-level causal transformer pretrained on about 1.29 million NYU patients to predict the next visit event set, with history-dependent downweighting of repeated events. A future-time separator token gives one-pass zero-shot onset risk at 2 and 5 years for seven diseases (macro AUROC 0.780 and 0.752), above next-token rollout baselines and a prompted LLM, and close to a fine-tuned BERT (0.767 and 0.757). Zero-shot EHRSHOT transfer is competitive on some tasks and below the fully supervised best on all six. Raw scores are miscalibrated until recalibrated. Classified L1, core, R3. Source points: only one-step use, horizon scores non-monotone, small positive counts in EHRSHOT, causal queries not addressed.
